name: People's Bank of China

leader.name: Pan Gongsheng
leader.title: Governor
leader.background: A veteran central banker and foreign-exchange regulator, Pan previously led SAFE and served as a PBOC deputy governor.

mandate: Maintain currency stability and thereby support economic growth.
facts: The 7-day reverse repo is a key policy-rate signal; the reserve requirement ratio also affects liquidity.
LPR is a lending benchmark based on bank quotations, not the PBOC’s own overnight policy rate.
The 5-year-plus LPR is important for mortgage pricing; both LPR tenors were unchanged at the 20 September fixing.
soWhat: Stable benchmark rates can coexist with liquidity injections. Watch the price of liquidity separately from the quantity supplied.

news.title: China keeps loan prime rates unchanged
news.summary: The official government report confirms unchanged 1-year and 5-year-plus lending benchmarks.
news.sourceName: People's Bank of China / State Council

news.title: 7-day operation remains at 1.40%
news.summary: The reported operation adds liquidity without changing the policy rate.
news.sourceName: People's Bank of China / State Council

sourceName: People's Bank of China / State Council
transmission: Liquidity operations, bank funding, LPRs and the renminbi.
watch: Credit demand, property support, LPR fixings and reserve-ratio signals.
teamRead: Traditionally growth-sensitive and state-coordinated; the present signal is a dovish tilt through liquidity support rather than a broad rate cut.
stanceNote: Benchmarks were held while liquidity support remained active. That mix reads as cautiously accommodative.

name: Reserve Bank of India

leader.name: Sanjay Malhotra
leader.title: Governor
leader.background: Sanjay Malhotra is a career civil servant who previously served as India’s Revenue Secretary and held senior finance and power-sector roles.

mandate: Maintain price stability while keeping growth in mind.
facts: The MPC sets the repo rate; the standing deposit facility is 5.00% and MSF / Bank Rate 5.50% in the verified snapshot.
RBI lists banks’ base rates at 8.40–10.00% and overnight MCLR at 7.80–8.00%; neither is one national prime rate.
Bank loan pricing may use external benchmarks plus borrower-specific spreads.
soWhat: An unchanged repo rate does not make every loan unchanged: reset dates, spreads and funding costs affect transmission.

news.title: MPC leaves repo rate unchanged
news.summary: RBI resolution reproduced by Track RBI: unanimous hold at 5.25%.

news.title: Current policy and lending-rate reference
news.summary: Official table separates policy rates, base rates, MCLR and deposit rates.

transmission: Repo-linked money-market rates, bank funding and loan benchmarks.
watch: Food inflation, core inflation, growth momentum and liquidity conditions.
teamRead: The MPC is data-dependent rather than structurally hawkish or dovish; its latest neutral stance balances inflation with growth.
stanceNote: An unchanged repo rate and neutral language imply no strong directional bias.

name: Monetary Authority of Singapore

leader.name: Chia Der Jiun
leader.title: Managing Director
leader.background: Chia Der Jiun previously served as Permanent Secretary at Singapore’s Ministry of Manpower and held senior roles at MAS, the Ministry of Finance and the Public Service Division.

mandate: Maintain price stability conducive to sustainable economic growth.
facts: MAS manages the Singapore dollar against a trade-weighted basket within a policy band.
It adjusts the band’s slope, width or centre; the precise parameters are not publicly disclosed.
SORA is a market overnight-rate benchmark, not an MAS policy target. Board chairman: Gan Kim Yong; managing director: Chia Der Jiun.
soWhat: Faster currency appreciation can restrain imported inflation, while affecting exporters and the translation of overseas earnings.

news.title: MAS announces senior leadership changes
news.summary: MAS announced senior management changes effective 1 November; Chia Der Jiun remains Managing Director.

news.title: MAS slightly steepens appreciation path
news.summary: Policy tightening works through the exchange rate rather than a numerical policy-rate increase.

news.title: What July’s calibrated tightening means
news.summary: DBS examines the small increase in the currency band’s slope.

transmission: A managed trade-weighted exchange rate changes imported inflation and competitiveness.
watch: Core inflation, imported costs, growth and the S$NEER band’s slope.
teamRead: MAS is pragmatic and forecast-led. The latest calibrated steepening gives the team a hawkish tilt without using an interest-rate target.
stanceNote: A slightly faster appreciation path is a measured tightening signal.

name: Bank of England

leader.name: Andrew Bailey
leader.title: Governor
leader.background: Andrew Bailey previously led the UK Financial Conduct Authority and served as the Bank’s Deputy Governor for prudential regulation and chief cashier.

mandate: Target 2% CPI inflation; subject to that, support government economic policy.
facts: The nine-member MPC decides Bank Rate. Three members preferred a 25 bp increase in September.
Bank Rate influences money-market and bank funding costs; retail mortgage rates also depend on expected future rates.
The UK has no single central-bank-set prime lending rate.
soWhat: A hold can still send a tightening signal. Businesses should watch the vote split and inflation outlook, not just the unchanged headline rate.

news.title: Bank Rate held at 3.75%
news.summary: The MPC kept the rate unchanged, with three votes for an increase.

news.title: Energy costs keep inflation risks in focus
news.summary: Reporting explains why the Bank remains alert to persistent price pressures.

transmission: Bank Rate and expectations feed into sterling, gilt yields, deposits and mortgages.
watch: Energy prices, wage setting, services inflation and second-round effects.
teamRead: The MPC is divided: the majority held, while three members preferred a hike. The collective signal is a hawkish tilt.
stanceNote: Holding amid three votes for a rise and stronger inflation warnings is hawkish relative to a simple hold.

name: European Central Bank

leader.name: Christine Lagarde
leader.title: President
leader.background: Christine Lagarde previously led the IMF and served as France’s finance minister; she is a lawyer by training rather than a career monetary economist.

mandate: Price stability: 2% inflation over the medium term.
facts: The ECB sets policy for the euro area—not all EU countries.
Main refinancing rate: 2.65%; marginal lending facility: 2.90%, effective 16 September.
The deposit facility rate steers policy; commercial lending rates differ across banks and countries.
soWhat: Higher euro rates can increase financing costs and affect the euro. Transmission can differ between member economies.

news.title: ECB raises its three key rates
news.summary: The deposit rate increases to 2.50%, effective 16 September.

news.title: Why a 2% medium-term target?
news.summary: Understand the symmetric inflation objective behind rate decisions.

transmission: Policy rates move euro money markets, bank funding, sovereign yields and the euro.
watch: Wage growth, services inflation, energy prices and differences in transmission across member states.
teamRead: The Governing Council’s latest rate increase and inflation language make the current team signal hawkish, though decisions remain meeting-by-meeting.
stanceNote: A 25 bp increase is an unambiguous tightening action.

name: US Federal Reserve

leader.name: Kevin Warsh
leader.title: Chairman
leader.background: Kevin Warsh previously served as a Federal Reserve governor and worked in investment banking and economic policy. His official testimony stresses price stability and policy credibility.

mandate: Maximum employment and stable prices; 2% longer-run PCE inflation goal.
facts: The FOMC sets a target range; the effective federal funds rate is an observed market rate.
Prime is a commercial-bank lending benchmark, not the Fed’s policy rate.
The September 18 H.15 release records a 7.00% prime rate for September 17.
soWhat: Tighter dollar funding can affect global borrowers, equity valuations and exchange rates, not only US households.

news.title: Fed raises its target range
news.summary: The FOMC raises the range by 25 bp to 3.75–4.00%.

news.title: Prime rate rises to 7.00%
news.summary: The official release separates prime lending, effective fed funds and Treasury yields.

transmission: Fed funds expectations move the dollar, Treasury yields, credit spreads and bank prime rates globally.
watch: Core inflation, payrolls, unemployment, demand resilience and inflation expectations.
teamRead: The 2026 FOMC includes varied regional and Board views, but its unanimous September hike makes the current collective signal hawkish.
stanceNote: A unanimous increase to support a faster return to 2% inflation is clearly hawkish.

name: Bank of Canada

leader.name: Tiff Macklem
leader.title: Governor
leader.background: Tiff Macklem previously served as the Bank’s senior deputy governor and as dean of the Rotman School of Management; he also worked at Canada’s Department of Finance.

mandate: Target 2% inflation within a 1–3% range; use flexibility to support sustainable employment.
facts: The overnight target differs from Bank Rate (2.50%) and the deposit rate (2.20%).
Each commercial bank sets its prime rate; the Bank of Canada publishes a major-bank reference.
Policy decisions weigh both inflation pressure and economic weakness.
soWhat: A stable policy rate need not mean stable financial conditions: trade uncertainty and credit spreads can still affect business investment.

news.title: Bank of Canada holds at 2.25%
news.summary: The Bank leaves its overnight target unchanged.

news.title: Deliberations highlight trade and inflation risks
news.summary: The discussion explains the balance between growth risks and inflation.

transmission: The overnight target influences Canadian money markets, bank prime rates, mortgages and the Canadian dollar.
watch: October 28 rate decision, energy inflation, tariffs and the durability of the economic rebound.
teamRead: The Governing Council balances inflation risk against economic weakness. The latest hold reads as balanced rather than strongly hawkish or dovish.
stanceNote: A hold with two-sided risks gives little directional conviction.
